llm.summary: The instructions mostly match the stated goal (creating an agent and wiring a channel) but the skill directs editing system-wide config under /root, storing/shared API keys and tokens in a global JSON, and does not declare or justify that level of access — this is coherent for setup but raises credential-exposure and privilege concerns.

dimensions.detail: Creating a workspace, adding an agent entry, and registering channel accounts in openclaw.json is consistent with 'create a new agent and connect a messaging channel'. However the guidance hardcodes /root paths and states that existing API keys are automatically shared across agents — both are notable design choices that broaden impact beyond a single agent and should be justified.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs the operator/agent to read and modify /root/.openclaw/openclaw.json, create persistent workspaces under /root, add channel bot tokens/service-account paths into the global config, and restart the gateway. Those actions are within the purpose but give the new agent and any other process with access to openclaw.json potential access to many credentials and global routing rules.

dimensions.detail: Instruction-only skill with no install step or downloaded code — lowest installer risk. There is no package or remote fetch to evaluate.

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required env vars/credentials yet instructs the user to place sensitive channel tokens and service account paths into a global config and states that existing auth profiles/keys are automatically shared. Requesting or relying on broad, implicit credential sharing (without declaring or restricting it) is disproportionate and increases credential exposure.

dimensions.detail: The skill modifies a system-wide configuration file (openclaw.json) and creates persistent workspace directories under /root, which affects other agents and the runtime. always is false (good), but modifying global routing/accounts increases blast radius and should be limited or gated.

llm.guidance: Before using this skill: 1) Review and back up /root/.openclaw/openclaw.json and confirm who can read it — it will contain bot tokens and possibly service-account paths. 2) Prefer running agent setup from a non-root user and use per-agent, least-privilege credentials where possible (avoid sharing high-privilege API keys across agents). 3) If adding Google service-account JSON or bot tokens, store them securely (encrypted, with restricted file permissions) rather than in plain global JSON. 4) Confirm that restarting the gateway and changing global bindings is acceptable for your environment (do this in a test environment first). 5) Ask the skill author how credentials are scoped and whether newly created agents can access existing platform API keys; if not satisfactory, refuse or require per-agent credential provisioning. 6) Rotate tokens/keys after testing and audit access logs to detect unexpected access.
